Black Man with Long History of Arrests, Arrested on Drug and Arms Charges [Ramelus D. Bradley] [Columbia MO]

No Cached Version

A federal grand jury on Monday indicted a 34-year-old Columbia man on drug trafficking and illegal firearm possession charges for an August incident, Tammy Dickinson, U.S. attorney for the Western District of Missouri, said in a news release.

Ramelus D. Bradley was charged with one count of possessing cocaine with the intent to distribute, one count of possessing crack cocaine with the intent to distribute and one count of illegally possessing a firearm. The indictment replaces a federal criminal complaint filed against Bradley in August.

Deputies raided Bradley’s apartment in the 4800 block of Prairie Circle on Aug. 21 and found Bradley standing within reach of three firearms, Dickinson said in the release. Deputies observed about 22 grams of marijuana at Bradley’s feet and found two infants in an upstairs bedroom, the release said.

Authorities reportedly seized four firearms and ammunition, about 22 grams of marijuana, about 6.5 ounces of cocaine, numerous unidentified pills and $12,258 in cash. Deputies also found an unspecified amount of marijuana that had been pre-packaged for sale as well as a digital scale with cocaine residue inside Bradley’s pickup truck, the release said.

Bradley has several misdemeanor and felony convictions in Missouri, according to online records. He has misdemeanor convictions for third-degree domestic assault, second-degree property damage, first-degree trespassing, driving while revoked and stealing. He has felony convictions for second-degree drug trafficking, possession of a controlled substance and two each for distribution of a controlled substance and resisting arrest.

As part of the indictment, Bradley would be required to forfeit the cash authorities seized and any property obtained using proceeds from the alleged offenses.
